chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Fadhal, from 'Uqbah, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Looking is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis, and how many a glance has caused long-lasting regret.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of looking in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describing the gaze as a 'poisoned arrow' from Iblis, emphasizing its active role in spiritual corruption rather than mere passive observation. This metaphor highlights the immediate and lingering consequences of the 'first glance,' which often serves as the gateway to deeper sins and enduring regret in Shia ethical tradition.
